title: data-objectstack README still tells readers to install @objectstack/client separately — the same claim #4127 corrected on the docs page
body:
Out-of-scope finding from #4124 (the phantom React API on the same package's docs page).

## Fact (verified on `origin/main` = `1b6188d41`)

`packages/data-objectstack/README.md:16` says:

```bash
npm install @object-ui/data-objectstack @objectstack/client
```

But `@objectstack/client` is a regular `dependency` of the package (`packages/data-objectstack/package.json`), not a peer — it is installed and resolved along with it. PR #4127 corrected exactly this claim on `content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx`, where the install line is now bare and the note reads "is a regular dependency ... nothing to install separately". The README was not in that card's scope, so it still carries the old wording.

## Why this is observation-class, not a defect

Following the README does not break anything: `@objectstack/client` is a real dependency, so installing it explicitly resolves to the same package. The cost is a reader being told the dependency contract is something it is not — the same misconception #3781 was filed to remove, surviving in the other of the two places that state it.

## Suggested fix

Match the docs page: drop `@objectstack/client` from the install command and, if a note is wanted, say it ships as a regular dependency.

Two adjacent spots in the same README worth a glance while there (not verified in depth):

- the `## Links` section points at `https://www.objectui.org/docs/guide/data-source`, which is fine;
- the README's own API Reference lists adapter methods and was NOT found to contain the `ObjectStackProvider` / `useObjectStack` fabrication that #4124 removed from the docs page — the README has always documented the real surface.

## Searched for duplicates

`README data-objectstack install peer dependency`, `data-objectstack README install separately client`, and a full `is:open data-objectstack` sweep (34 open issues) over this repo: no existing card covers the README's install line. #4125 covers a stale version string on the docs pages, which is a different site.
